Our new Managing Director, Neil Fleming.

We are thrilled to announce that Neil Fleming has been appointed as our New Managing Director. 

Neil started with us in March 2016 when we were appointed as the New Head of Landscaping. His extensive experience in commercial landscaping resulted in sharp growth of that area of our business.

In 2021, Neil was promoted to Chief Operating Officer (COO), requiring him to work closely with both areas of our business, landscape and building management.

During this period, he developed strong relationships with clients, suppliers and other stakeholders making him influential in our business, enabling him to progress his career to Managing Director. 

Mark Noakes, who acquired IPM Facilities Ltd in 2015, now hands over the day to day running of the business to Neil. Mark will continue to be a key part of our company and moves into his new role as CEO. 

He will support Neil and the other senior management team to ensure the business continues to thrive.

“Neil's practical approach, operational expertise, and customer focus have helped him develop quickly and coupled with great leadership, has resulted in real development for our business.” said Mark.

Over the last four years, we have had significant growth – both financially and geographically, with turnover increasing by 50% and the landscape and property management of over 250 new properties.

Neil commented, “I feel privileged to be appointed as MD of a great Company. I am proud of IPM Facilities, its achievements and its ethos and feel very lucky to have such an amazing team around me. 

During my nine years here, I have seen the Company go from strength to strength. Excellent service provision has been the key, and I will continue to drive that forward”

Congratulations Neil.

post.post_text:
Despite the shock and fallout from the news ISG staff received on Thursday, it is no surprise at all to see the incredible gathering round, support and concern for each other on linkedin and other platforms. In my time at ISG I have met , worked and become close friends with a huge number of highly motivated, knowledgeable and talented people across a range of disciplines and levels of experience in Work Winning and Precon- people who as late as Thursday evening and Friday morning were working hard for what everyone expected to be a brighter year ahead for the business.

And despite the brutal cut off, it is clear that colleagues will carry that team spirit and collective support that made ISG such a great place to work, forward into wherever their next chapter takes them.  

A huge thanks from me to all ISG colleagues I have had the pleasure to work with over the past four and a half years- many of whom I now won't be able to reach other than via Linked in- pretty much universally it has been an absolute joy and an education. Best of luck to everyone in their search for alternative positions- stay positive and back yourselves, the projects and opportunities are still out there and the industry is driven by recognised talent being snapped up and put to good use- I am certain the colleagues I know well will all go on to greater things- taking their ISG experience and imbuing that same culture and spirit into wherever they go. If anyone I have worked with needs anything from me to help in job hunting going forward, please don't hesitate to ask. 

Also thanks to all the consultants, clients and supply chain partners I have worked with in this time- we did some great work, often against very challenging odds, to deliver quality projects for other people's staff, pupils and parents, teachers and other building users. I hope you will all strive to keep the same teams together wherever possible to see current projects through. There is always the risk of knowledge loss in the re-allocating of live projects with such an abrupt cutoff, so again if anyone wants to pick my brain on anything (for what it's worth), you just need to drop me a line.

For now, I am looking to step back a bit, take stock and take my time to consider what's next for a quieter life. For those of you who are thinking "Aye, right!", you probably know me better than I know myself!

post.post_text:
And there it was.. 

Last week marked the end of my time at Mace.  I found Mace (or they found me?!) in 2011. It’s been some adventure since then. I was only meant to be there for 2 weeks at the end of Jaunary 2011. And after 7 different roles and 11 years, August 2022 was the time to move on. 

Firstly, full credit to ALL of the incredible Mace people I’ve met along that journey. The doers. The creators. The late night grafters. The engineers. The builders. The academics. The innovators. Thank you. It was you that made it the fun and rewarding experience it was. “People buy people” was an early catchphrase of mine, and bringing a bit more humanity and humility into the workplace has built stronger relationships and achieved better things. I’m grateful to have had the space to do that with so many.  

There were a lot of successes over the 11 years, We won awards. All of the awards. Secured amazing contracts in amazing parts of the world, and delivered them in style. And the greatest successes of them all on reflection were the personal ones. The people I’ve worked with to overcome adversity. To take a big step. To try something unexpected. The quote around how the most meaningful way to succeed is to help others to succeed definitely resonates following a month of goodbyes and good wishes. 

There’s also big regrets. I’ve encountered loss, tragedy, and misfortune in 11 years. That’s possibly the nature of being in a big organisation and knowing a lot of people. Possibly not. Time moves on. The good memories, and stories, keep spirits high and legacies alive.  

A big part of the role has been the clients, partners and suppliers we worked with along the way. And the change we delivered together. It’s an honour to have worked with some of the startups and founders I have over the years. And being a part of programmes like Construction Innovation Hub, the @construction productivity taskforce and Infrastructure Industry Innovation Partnership (i3P)  has highlighted both how collaboration is key, and progress can happen at pace. 

And progress we must. Accelerating the response to the climate emergency. And transforming the construction industry. There’s plenty still to do.  

I genuinely could not recommend Mace highly enough to anyone. I’ve always happily said it’s the best place I’ve ever worked. A place where if you have the ideas and the initiative you can make it happen. And will be supported to make it happen. For anyone keen to make an impact in the world, and looking for that next challenge, there’s few better places…

Onwards. And upwards. To you all. Together we got this.

The last four years on the Alexander Stadium Redevelopment has been a roller coaster of a journey! We've had challenges thrown at us which no-one could have predicted and i've been pushed mentally, physically and emotionally, yet throughout the entire project the team dynamic, values and collaboration has been a true example of how projects can be delivered. 

From the design phase, construction and through the recent facility management delivery, each member has played a vital role on the project and i'm proud to have met so many incredible people. Seeing the stadium in action is a true testament to how important this facility will be for the people of Birmingham moving forward. Whilst we can celebrate it being delivered to budget and time, it will be the lasting legacy which will truly define the projects success.
